body:
Craft open (round 1): three small, shippable ideas aimed at rule/CLI architecture — not dangertape/lockplain. Prefer a single source of truth for rule metadata, kill duplicated severity logic, and one high-signal added-line heuristic.

C1 (--list-rules): rules() is closed today; help/glossary can drift from src/rules.ts. Export a catalog (id/severity/title/score) and print it from CLI so CI triage and docs stay honest.

C2 (rule severity SSOT): large-diff computes severity inside test() then runRules recomputes; hotspot-paths uses score:0 and re-walks HOTSPOT_PATTERNS. Return severity+score from test (or compute once) so Finding fields cannot diverge.

C3 (conflict-markers rule): same added-line scan pattern as todo-fix/config-bypass; catch leftover <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> — tiny, high precision, no sibling overlap. Optionally extract shared addedLines(patch) while touching those three sites.

ideas.title: --list-rules exports heuristic catalog
ideas.note: src/rules.ts: export listRules()/RULE_CATALOG (id, severity, title, score). src/cli.ts: --list-rules early exit like --version. README/glossary: sync from same catalog. Why: single source of truth; CI triage without scraping help; not helpgate.

ideas.title: Unify rule severity/score in one path
ideas.note: src/rules.ts runRules + large-diff/hotspot-paths tests: stop double-computing severity/score (test returns it OR runRules owns it, not both). Why: avoids silent drift when thresholds change; score:0 + re-scan of HOTSPOT_PATTERNS is a maintenance bug waiting to happen.

ideas.title: conflict-markers heuristic on added lines
ideas.note: src/rules.ts: new rule id conflict-markers (high/critical) scanning added lines for <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>; extract tiny addedLines(patch) helper shared with todo-fix/config-bypass/secret-patterns. Why: real merge residue, tiny surface, fits existing rule shape; do not expand lockfile lane.

body: Revising toward the majority single idea. @product: I support P1 (--list-rules) as the one shippable winner — CI triage reliability beats adding another heuristic this pass, and your ranking (discoverability first) is right for one idea. @craft: C1 is the right shape (export catalog from rules.ts, early-exit CLI); my reliability caveat is that the printed severity/title/score must come from the same objects runRules uses — no hand-maintained parallel list — so we do not invent a second SSOT (C2 can wait; do not expand this pass into severity unification). @experience: E1 over E3 for this round — I still like exclude for grade honesty (my R2), but it is a bigger CLI/filter surface and can wait; --list-rules is smaller and unblocks operators who currently cannot map fail-on findings to rule ids without reading source. Parking R1 conflict-markers (and R3 debug-leftovers): still high-signal merge hazards, but three seats already converge on list-rules; R1 should be next pass after catalog exists so the new rule id is listable on day one. Stance: for P1/C1/E1 as THE idea; against picking conflict-markers as the sole winner this round.
